html:
Harry Thuku was a Kikuyu activist who led one of the first modern political movements in Kenya, protesting against forced labour, high taxes and the kipande pass that African men had to carry.

A clerk in Nairobi, he founded the Young Kikuyu Association and then the East African Association in 1921. He was arrested in March 1922, and a crowd gathered at the police station to demand his release. When Mary Muthoni Nyanjiru taunted the men to act, police and settlers opened fire, killing a number of people, among them Nyanjiru herself.

Thuku was exiled to the north until 1930, and later became a moderate. His movement was a forerunner of the nationalism of Jomo Kenyatta and of protest against the settler order.
sum: Harry Thuku was a Kikuyu activist who led one of the first modern political movements in Kenya, protesting against forced labour, high taxes and the kipande pass that African men had to carry.
